# Relative compound labels against the real Pirelli compound

Leave-one-race-out within-stint R², the Result 1 protocol at each
circuit's published degree, with the tyre coded two ways: the relative
label (Soft/Medium/Hard) and the compound Pirelli nominated (C0-C6, the
2022 C1 coded C0). Both are scored on the same laps.

The allocation changed between seasons at 16 of 24 circuits; elsewhere the two codings are the same model. At those circuits the median score moves from 0.003 to -0.033, a median difference of -0.008 (95% interval over circuits [-0.177, +0.001]). The real compound scores better at 5, worse at 11 (sign test p = 0.21), and its largest gain anywhere is +0.017.

With every circuit forced to the linear model, so that no quadratic can
extrapolate on a compound seen in one season only: median difference -0.003 ([-0.021, +0.001]), better at 6, worse at 10 (p = 0.45).

On average 2.8% of a held-out season's laps at those circuits are on a compound no other season used (at most 10.7% at one circuit), and the real coding cannot predict them at all.
